- Primary asks: private connectivity (PrivateLink vs VPC peering), IP allowlists/static egress, and data residency in us-west-2.
- Expected traffic: ~120 qps, burst to 300 qps during peak daily windows; avg request size ~350 tokens.

Open items / asks from your side:
1) Confirm preferred connectivity approach (AWS PrivateLink vs cross-account VPC Peering).
2) Provide VPC CIDR(s) and whether you can accept cross-account peering or prefer endpoint service model.
3) Any requirement for fixed egress IPs to implement IP allowlists on your side?
4) Security asks: will your team need SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration details?

I've attached a high-level VPC architecture diagram (vpc-architecture.png) and a short provisioning checklist (provisioning-checklist.pdf) that outlines information we typically need from customers to stand up PrivateLink/peering.

Next steps I propose:
- If you prefer PrivateLink, schedule 30m with our infra engineer (Dev) and your network/security contact to walk through the endpoint provisioning flow.
- If you prefer peering, we'll need your AWS account ID and target VPC CIDRs to validate no overlapping ranges.

Proposed windows: Thu 7/15 9:00-11:00 PT or 2:00-4:00 PT. Let me know what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Marissa

Perfect — 9:30 PT works. I'll send a 30-min invite in a minute. Invite will include a short agenda: confirm CIDRs, discuss PrivateLink vs peering flow, and list of artifacts/security deliverables.

To answer your peering question: if we do VPC peering we will provide our account ID and an AWS-side target VPC (non-overlapping CIDR). For PrivateLink we publish a service in our account and you'll create an Interface VPC Endpoint in yours — that avoids peering but requires you to create ENIs in your subnets. Both options are supported; PrivateLink is typically preferred for stricter security postures.

For static egress IPs: we can offer NAT-ing through a pair of static egress IPs (or an Elastic IP pool) in the deployment region — will confirm the exact addresses during provisioning.

I'll attach the provisioning checklist to the calendar invite and loop in our solutions engineer (Dev) to lead the technical discussion.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the details. A few technical clarifications ahead of the 9:30 call so we can make it productive:

1) CIDR overlap check: your stated ranges (10.40.0.0/16 and 10.41.0.0/16) look good. If you plan to use a transit VPC, let us know whether traffic will egress from the transit VPC or the application VPC.

2) Peering vs PrivateLink:
   - PrivateLink (Interface VPC Endpoint): recommended for strict security. You will create an ENI in each AZ; this requires subnets with available IPs. We will provide the service name and our account ID at the start of provisioning.
   - VPC Peering: simpler for cross-account routing but requires non-overlapping CIDRs and route table updates. No ENIs in your account required.

3) Static egress IPs: if you require allowlisting outbound IPs, we can place traffic through a NAT gateway pair with Elastic IP(s) or a static egress proxy — we should agree whether you want a small pool (2–4 IPs) or a larger range.

4) TLS/KMS: we terminate TLS at the endpoint; we can integrate with customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest if required. Please note there are additional procurement steps for customer-managed keys that we'll include in the provisioning checklist.

Before the call please send:
- The AWS account ID you're happy to use for connectivity (or confirm you want to use PrivateLink).
- Subnet IDs in the AZs you'd prefer for interface endpoints (if choosing PrivateLink).
- Any firewall/proxy that could block outbound connections to our service domain.

I'll bring a sample endpoint configuration and a short runbook to the call.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
